lesson.title: Motion Graphs: Mail Carrier Mystery
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 1 Lesson 1: Motion Graphs - Mail Carrier Mystery

gradingDesign.rule: All variable student evidence is graded only in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: On a position-time graph, what does a steeper upward slope mean?
Which pair of graph features represents an object that is stopped?
A truck's velocity is -4 m/s. What does the negative sign show?
Which graph combination represents constant positive velocity?
What must happen to velocity when an object turns around and begins moving in the opposite direction?
A mail truck moves from x = 10 m to x = 34 m in 6 s. What is its average velocity in m/s?
A truck starts at x = 5 m, travels to x = 25 m, and returns to x = 9 m. What is its displacement in meters?
For the same trip from 5 m to 25 m and back to 9 m, what total distance did the truck travel in meters?
Choose one case from the Motion Graph Explorer. Describe the truck's motion and cite one matching feature from both its position-time graph and its velocity-time graph.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Use a named explorer case and connect the same motion interval to evidence from both graphs.
a. Full credit: Names a case, accurately describes the motion, and cites a matching position-time feature and velocity-time feature from the same interval.
  Partial credit: Correctly describes the motion but gives clear evidence from only one graph, or discusses both graphs without naming a case.
  No credit: Gives no identifiable case, contradicts the displayed graphs, or provides no graph evidence.

questions.prompt: Compare two different Motion Graph Explorer cases. Explain how a stop or direction change appears differently on a position-time graph and a velocity-time graph, and use specific evidence from both cases.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] A strong comparison identifies two cases, explains slope and velocity sign, and uses evidence from both graph types.
a. Full credit: Identifies two cases, accurately compares their motion, explains how a stop or reversal changes position-time slope and velocity-time value or sign, and cites specific graph evidence from both cases.
  Partial credit: Gives a generally correct comparison but omits one graph type, one case, or the connection between slope and velocity sign.
  No credit: Discusses fewer than two cases, treats position and velocity as the same quantity, or gives no relevant evidence.
